title: Running AI agents safely on a cluster
blurb: How to let a learning agent use the real internet without letting it do real damage: sandboxes, egress proxies, logging and staged rollouts.
description: Reinforcement learning agents learn by acting, often with a terminal and the internet. The film explains how a research cluster works, what an RL rollout looks like, eight concrete failure modes, and a safety design: strong sandboxes, default-deny networking through a proxy, logging outside the box, canary tokens, a kill switch and a staged rollout.
takeaways: On a cluster your job runs as you, and the machine is shared, so you are responsible for what your agents do.
A sandbox is only as safe as what is mounted in it, so a good rollout sandbox starts empty.
Never give one rollout private data, untrusted content and a way to send information out at the same time.
Training searches for whatever earns reward, so loopholes in the checker will be found and must be closed.
Move up from no network to a frozen web mirror to a small allowlist only after the lower stage has run clean.
